newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam's economy gets mixed bill of health.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam's economy gets mixed bill of health.

text.p: Vietnam is on track to meet most of its economic targets this year, but a government minister has indicated concern about problems with budget revenue collection and a yawning trade gap, state media said on Tuesday.
Le Xuan Trinh, Hanoi's Government Office Minister, told a news conference on Monday that annual inflation was expected to end the year at around six to seven percent, down from 12.7 percent in 1995.
He added that annual gross domestic product (GDP) growth was expected to meet a target of 9.5 percent while food output would reach 28.2 million tonnes, up from 1995's 27.5 million.
But in other areas, he indicated Vietnam's end-of-year economic report would be less rosy.
He said revenue collection -- a government priority this year -- was facing "many difficulties", with income from taxes and debt repayment at just 53 percent of the year's target in August.
Hanoi, whose 1995 budget deficit has been estimated by the International Monetary Fund at 1.7 percent of GDP, does not publish details of government spending and revenues.

Trinh added that additional efforts were needed to boost industrial production and tackle a fast-growing trade gap, which stood at a record $3.25 billion in the first eight months of this year compared with $2.3 billion for the whole of 1995.

"Exports should be speeded up," the Quan Doi Nhan Dan newspaper quoted him as saying. "...Imports of unnecessary items which are produced in Vietnam such as cement and consumer goods...should be limited to keep the trade balance."
Further details were not given. Foreign correspondents were not invited to attend the news conference.
